subject: psychology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Research methods (experiments, observations, surveys, interviews, correlational studies, case studies)
Research considerations (reliability, validity, generalisability, bias, reflexivity, credibility)

questions.q: An experiment can support a causal claim because the researcher:
options: Manipulates an independent variable and controls extraneous variables
Measures two variables as they vary
questions.explain: Manipulation plus control lets changes in the DV be attributed to the IV.

questions.q: The variable a researcher deliberately changes is the:
questions.explain: The IV is manipulated; the DV is measured.

questions.q: A correlational study can show a relationship but cannot:
options: Establish that one variable causes another
questions.explain: Correlation shows association; causation needs experimental manipulation.

questions.q: An in-depth investigation of a single individual or group is a:
questions.explain: Case studies give rich, holistic data on one case, often using multiple methods.

questions.q: A semi-structured interview:
options: Uses core questions plus freedom to probe
questions.explain: It balances consistency with flexibility to explore responses.

questions.q: To understand, in depth, how patients experience a treatment, the best method is:
questions.explain: Lived experience and meaning are best explored through qualitative interviewing.

questions.q: A naturalistic observation studies behaviour:
questions.explain: Naturalistic observation has high ecological validity but less control.

questions.q: In a random sample, every member of the target population has:
options: To be chosen by the researcher
questions.explain: Random sampling improves representativeness by giving equal selection probability.

questions.q: Opportunity sampling selects participants who are:
questions.explain: Opportunity sampling uses whoever is accessible, which risks bias.

questions.q: A limitation of volunteer (self-selected) samples is that they:
questions.explain: Volunteers may differ systematically from the population, limiting generalisability.

questions.q: Purposive sampling selects participants because they:
options: Have characteristics relevant to the research question
questions.explain: Purposive sampling targets information-rich cases, common in qualitative work.

questions.q: A researcher advertises and uses those who respond. This is:
questions.explain: Volunteers responding to an advert form a self-selected sample.

questions.q: A larger, more representative sample mainly improves:
questions.explain: Representative samples let findings apply more confidently to the population.

questions.q: Reliability refers to the ___ of a measure or result.
questions.explain: Reliability is consistency; validity is whether it measures what it claims to.

questions.q: Ecological validity concerns whether findings:
questions.explain: Ecological validity is about how far results apply beyond the study setting.

questions.q: Reflexivity means the researcher:
options: Reflects on how their own role and assumptions shape the research
questions.explain: Reflexivity acknowledges and examines the researcher's influence, aiding credibility.

questions.q: In qualitative research, 'credibility' broadly parallels which quantitative criterion?
questions.explain: Within trustworthiness criteria, credibility parallels internal validity.

questions.q: Demand characteristics occur when participants:
options: Guess the aim and change their behaviour
questions.explain: Cues can lead participants to infer the aim and respond accordingly, threatening validity.

questions.q: To reduce demand characteristics, a researcher could:
options: Use a cover story, then debrief
questions.explain: A mild cover story reduces tailoring to the aim; a full debrief addresses the ethics.

questions.q: Triangulation strengthens a study by:
options: Cross-checking findings across methods, data or researchers
questions.explain: Triangulation improves credibility by corroborating findings from multiple angles.
